claims.statement: Capture ownership is recorded as a singleton instance ID plus database OID and PostgreSQL system identifier; mismatches or existing quarantine fail closed, and identity matching alone cannot distinguish physical copies preserving both identifiers.

Identity mismatch quarantines capture and suspends stream tables not already suspended with needs_reinit and CDC_CLONE_DETECTED; scheduler dispatch and ready-asserting API entrypoints refuse non-ready capture gates.

quiesce signals a drain and only persists QUIESCED after completion, returning false on unavailable signaling or timeout; pause_all aliases a 60-second quiesce, and resume_all restores ACTIVE but rejects quarantine.

Explicit capture adoption creates a new instance identity and clears quarantine but leaves every stream suspended, unpopulated, needing reinitialization with a null frontier; it does not remap dependency OIDs.

Capture adoption rotates output-delta log identity, invalidates non-dropped consumers with DATABASE_INSTANCE_CHANGED, and deletes outstanding resnapshot records while retaining old batches and cursors for a new baseline.

capture_instance_status reads stored state, whereas validate_recovery runs the identity gate and checks source existence, trigger availability, buffer registration/relation/schema, required WAL slots and lost WAL, and persisted frontier LSNs.

Missing triggers, slots, WAL, or buffers and corrupt buffer schema require reinitialization, while clone detection and the reserved interrupted-repair failure classify as operator intervention; current interrupted-repair representation is a taxonomy entry rather than a durable repair journal.
A persisted source frontier ahead of pg_current_wal_lsn suspends the stream with RECOVERY_FRONTIER_UNPROVEN and requires rebuilding rather than silently advancing or clamping the frontier.

Missing sources produce dependency BLOCKER checks and suspend affected streams, but current validate_recovery top-level aggregation only recognizes quarantine and REINITIALIZATION_REQUIRED before defaulting to SAFE, so individual checks must be inspected.

repair_stream_table requires a ready capture owner and caller ownership, orders source locks before advisory/catalog locks, verifies publication binding, resets private state and frontiers, and attempts reconstruction of missing capture infrastructure.

Repair rejects missing dependencies, can prohibit storage replacement under publication contracts, rebuilds IMMEDIATE storage under source locks, leaves deferred streams needing full rebuilding, and clears error/fuse state to restore refresh eligibility.
reinitialize_stream_table reuses repair and protected ALTER QUERY rebuilding for output-schema evolution; neither it nor repair automatically reconciles logical-restore source OID changes.
Scheduler crash recovery marks refresh-history records left RUNNING as FAILED with an interruption message because unfinished refresh transactions were rolled back by PostgreSQL.

change_buffer_durability defaults to logged, supports unlogged buffers that lose crash persistence and require full refresh, and sync logged buffers with synchronous_commit on; unlogged_buffers remains a compatibility alias.

For populated streams not already needing reinitialization, the scheduler validates required buffer state; missing sentinels reveal crash truncation or damage and validation failure marks the stream for full reinitialization.

Stable CDC object names support naming continuity but source registrations and synthetic sentinels remain source-identity-bound, so stable names are not automatic OID reconciliation or recovery of lost change rows.

Logical dumps retain durable configuration and dependency/CDC catalog rows under config-dump policy, exclude private window-state rows and WAL replication slots, and do not provide an automatic capture-resume contract.

The supported OID-shifted logical restore workflow stops scheduling and writes, exports definitions, adopts changed capture ownership, recreates the DAG in dependency order, and rebuilds/validates capture rather than guessing old-to-new relation mappings.
Physical backups may preserve relation identities and runtime capture state, but restore or promotion still requires identity, slot/WAL, and frontier validation before writes and scheduling resume.
pg_trickle_dump exports stream creation/configuration SQL in topological dependency order from catalog definitions and selected policies, not source data, WAL resources, or runtime checkpoint state.

Stream snapshots are ordinary relations registered in pgt_snapshots with version, frontier, and time metadata; restore validates relation/catalog provenance, expected stream identity, version compatibility, caller access, and output layout rather than trusting a same-named table.

Snapshot restore uses an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE storage lock and an internal subtransaction for truncation, explicit-column insertion, and frontier restoration, rolling back failures; when frontier metadata exists it restores the frontier and population state without itself proving retained subsequent CDC history or restoring consumers.

Fresh installation uses pgrx-generated entrypoint SQL and extension_sql definitions, while existing installations depend on hand-authored migrations, so changing Rust/fresh-install definitions alone does not maintain upgrade parity.

check_upgrade_completeness.sh statically compares new generated install SQL, an optional old baseline, and the upgrade script to detect omitted new SQL objects and columns; its name-based checks do not establish semantic equivalence.

catalog_manifest.py produces normalized live manifests and diffs covering schemas, relations, columns, constraints, indexes, routines, views, event triggers, extension membership, and config-dump policy, including normalization of extension owner.

Safe release changes require version synchronization through check-version-sync and review of compiled package, installed extension, and pgt_schema_version coherence; SQL parity must include security and dump-policy boundaries.

The 0.108.2 to 0.108.3 migration nulls row identity/probe versions and forces stream reinitialization, while its output-delta contract guard prevents incompatible changes with live consumers unless the allowed invalidation/resnapshot conditions hold.

Upgrade preflight reports blockers for quarantine, suspended/error/reinitializing streams and invalid catalog identities, recommends drain for jobs/backlog, warns on version mismatch, and always requires external disk-headroom review.

Focused failure tests cover timeout, cancellation, cleanup, repeated-error recovery, identity mismatch/adoption, locked-heartbeat progress, quiesce/resume, missing triggers/slots, and future-frontier failure schedules.

UNLOGGED buffer tests cover configuration, creation, conversion/idempotence, and compatibility rather than a complete power-loss/promotion matrix; the dump test specifically demonstrates OID-shifted two-level DAG recreation with scheduling stopped.

Upgrade tests cover catalog/function/version/dump-policy parity and persisted state, but several chain/drain cases are ignored by default; the major-version-named test only runs preflight/quiesce/resume, and the identity-upgrade fixture uses current code with historical SQL and seeded old-format state rather than an old library.
